finding.claim: Public URLs are built by concatenating an un-encoded normalized path onto the configured prefix. Dot-segments that survive normalization (e.g. %2e%2e) and query/fragment characters (? #) are passed through unchanged, so the generated URL can address a different resource than the stored key when the app passes user-influenced names and the CDN/origin decodes or interprets them. Low confidence: exploitability depends on the caller and the deployment.
finding.source: Caller-supplied path string to Filesystem::publicUrl() (e.g. a user-chosen filename), reaching src/Filesystem.php:192-202
finding.sink: PathPrefixer::prefixPath() concatenation in src/UrlGeneration/PrefixPublicUrlGenerator.php:21 producing the returned public URL (src/PathPrefixer.php:26)

trace.note: publicUrl() normalizes the path via pathNormalizer->normalizePath()
Only \p{C} control characters are rejected; %2e%2e, ?, #, % pass through
Literal '..' segments are collapsed or rejected; percent-encoded dot-segments are not literal '..' and survive
Normalized path handed to the URL generator without encoding
prefix . ltrim($path,'\/') concatenation, no percent-encoding or decoding
Same unencoded concatenation on the sharded path

finding.guards_checked: WhitespacePathNormalizer: rejects \p{C} characters (line 25-29) and literal '..' escaping the root (line 39-42); PathPrefixer: strips leading slashes (line 26); no percent-decoding or URL encoding exists anywhere in the tree; the caller-side encoding cannot be checked because callers are outside this tree; the adapter is absent from the tree so storage-key handling was not assessed.
